rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Special Spaces (Instant Effects) 2 Mid Game Scoring (after 3rd and 4th rounds) 3 End Game Scoring: Overview Welcome to the most exclusive gala night of the year! The most renowned luxury hoarders have already arrived, eager to exchange irresistible offers... and screw each other over to build the best collection of all. We were just waiting for you to start... The Great Split! In The Great Split, your goal is to build the most prestigious collection of riches. Each round, you split your hand of cards into two groups, put them into the wallet, and pass to the left player. At the same time, you receive a wallet from the player on your right. When you receive a wallet, you must choose which of the two groups of cards you want to pick, and give back the other. Then the original wallet is returned to you; completing your hand of cards for the round. Your hand contains cards you've picked from the player to your right, and those returned to you by the player on your left. Apply the effects of your cards to add to your collections. If a card shows more than 1 seal icon, you may either apply their effects on the same track or on different tracks. The Splitter Card acts as a wild. The Star Seals with white tails are wild seals and can be applied to any seal track. At any point, you may ignore the icons and advance 1 space either on the Gold Track or the Prestige Track. (BGA presents this option to you for every card, so don't worry about forgetting) Special Spaces (Instant Effects) When advancing on tracks, you may unlock further advancements if you reach or pass a special space. Gold Track: If you reach or move past a space with the double arrow icon, you immediately advance 2 space on a SINGLE other track of you choice (not the gold track itself). Seal Racks: If you reach or pass a space with a Resource icon, you immediately advance 1 space on the corresponding Resource track. Mid Game Scoring (after 3rd and 4th rounds) There are 4 kinds of Scoring tokens: the Tome, Artwork, and Gem Scorings. The fourth scoring token is a blank No Scoring token and has no effect. When a scoring line is crossed, the 2 scoring tokens placed on it are scored immediately. Purple Tome: The most advanced space reached or passed with the Prestige value banner is the amount of Prestige points you receive. The max possible is 10 Brown Artwork: Compare the current level of your Artwork Track with the position of the Market slider shown on the center board.. You gain Prestige points equal to the value shown on the Art Market slider. Options are [0, 6, 10, 13, or 15] Gems Scoring: Only the gem track LEAST advanced gets scored . These gems are considered more rare and valuable to you. Whichever gem scores gets multiplied by 2. End Game Scoring: The player with the most Prestige points wins. In case of a tie, the victory is shared... or should we say split? Points already earned during the game are included in the final tally. The following get added. Purple Tome: the most advanced space which you've reached or passed with the Prestige value banner is the amount of points you get. The max possible is 10 Brown Artwork: Compare the current level of your Artwork Track with the position of the Market slider shown. You gain Prestige points equal to the value show on the Art Market slider. Options are [0, 6, 10, 13, or 15] Gem Scoring: Only the gem track LEAST advanced gets scored because these gems are considered more rare and valuable to you. Whichever gem scores gets multiplied by 2. Contract Scoring for each track: Count the number of icons (including from your character sheet) and multiply by the prestige banner you've reached or passed. Purple Tome and Brown Artwork: max multiplier is 4 Gems and Coins: max multiplier is 3.

[Rating: 2.5/10] A track advancement game where you can interact with your neighbours through an 'I cut, you choose' mechanism. It reminded me of 7 Wonders, a game I cooled on the last time I played it. But this unbelievably bland and soulless affair makes 7 Wonders look like a masterpiece.

[Rating: 3/10] too much track management. Otherwise, the I-split-you-choose mechanism would have been great, if not latch onto such a boring mechanism.

[Rating: 3/10] Muy flojo, basado en una producción bonita y un gimmick a la hora de jugar.  Luego es que hay muy poco juego, hay quien dice que lo que pasa es que es familiar... a mi me parece que un juego sea diseñado para un publico poco exigente no puede ser excusa para colar cualquier cosa. Poca variabilidad y decisiones muy poco interesante, creo que se quemara en un par de partidas y nadie hablará de él en 6 meses.

[Rating: 3/10] Finished last out of 7 players, so that is why it is only 3. Have nice day, Internet strangers!

[Rating: 3/10] Draft with neighbours using an "I split, you choose" mechanism (split some to left, choose some from right). In theory the "split" in particular is an interesting decision, but the cards just move players up 10 aggressively uninteresting tracks (plus a VP track) on pointlessly overproduced player boards.  It's polished within an inch of its life. The drafting part works well but they left out all the sharp edges, like penalties for busting that would've opened the door to a bit of light extortion or a shared board that might have done something interesting to values. It's not broken, just unbe

[Rating: 3/10] Lo de dividir las cartas está bien, pero lo que se hace con ellas y lo que propone el juego es aburridísimo. Sin ganas de repetir.

[Rating: 3/10] Not for me - no theme, no excitement, no feel-good or feel-clever moments, just a bunch of moving cubes up and totaling them. Production is great but gameplay is dull as anything.

[Rating: 3/10] Played on BGA.  Very simple idea with too many scoring options that lead to too much math for very little fun.

[Rating: 3/10] Dull. The core split/drafting mechanic is fab, but the tracks are dreadful. We couldn't think of anything better than this?

[Rating: 3/10] Since you never know how your neighbor will evaluate your split, it feels safest to even out your splits as well as you can. In the end, I feel like I’m just moving cubes along bland scoring tracks—not playing mind games or testing new strategies.

[Rating: 4/10] Had a test game at Spiel 22. I was very disappointed from the game. the mechanic is nice, but the game is quite shallow, and repeats the same step again and again... not enough for me. Art-wise its fantastic.

[Rating: 4/10] "I split, you choose" based drafting game with each neighbour. The decisions on how to split the cards being pretty much the whole game. The theme did not come through at all, so felt very, very abstract with the tracks being very boring. Not enough for me at all.
